title: The Unexpected Yearbook
premise: Petra Villalobos, a scholarship student at Ashford Preparatory Academy, has survived two years by being forgettable—until history teacher Ms. Okonkwo pairs him with his tormentor, golden-boy Theo Marsh, for a semester project documenting the school's centennial. Digging through old yearbooks in the archive, Petra discovers a pattern of erased students: scholarship kids who left mid-year, their photos whited out, their names missing from records. As he and Theo trace the disappearances to a donor family that has quietly bought the school's silence for decades, Petra must choose between exposing the truth—which implicates Theo's grandfather and shatters their fragile alliance before prom—or protecting the one person who finally sees him. He publishes the yearbook's hidden pages the night of prom, costing him Theo's friendship but winning justice for the erased students and, at last, a place he belongs.
about_author: Cyrus Ashgrove is a former boarding school archivist who spent three years cataloging decades of student records before turning to fiction. He writes stories about outsiders who refuse to stay quiet, drawing on his belief that every institution keeps at least one locked drawer.

chapters.title: Head Down, Grades Up
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. We meet Petra navigating Ashford Prep's social minefield: he eats lunch in the library, deflects Theo Marsh's casual cruelties, and counts down days to graduation. When Ms. Okonkwo announces paired centennial projects—and reads his name beside Theo's—the classroom goes silent. Emotional beat: dread, the sick feeling of invisibility failing.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Forced collaboration begins badly: Theo does nothing, Petra does everything, resentment simmers. Sorting dusty yearbooks in the basement archive, Petra notices something odd—a 1987 photo with a face carefully inked out. Theo catches him staring and, surprisingly, doesn't mock him. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity replacing hostility.

chapters.title: Whited Out
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They find more: six students across four decades, each vanished from records mid-senior year. Theo recognizes a surname—his grandfather was head trustee then. He wants to stop; Petra can't. Their first real argument ends with an uneasy truce: finish the project, nothing more. Emotional beat: the pull between safety and obsession.

chapters.title: The Scholarship List
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Cross-referencing financial aid records, Petra realizes all six erased students were scholarship kids like him. A retired librarian, Mrs. Adeyemi, remembers one: a girl who 'left suddenly' after complaining about the Hollis family's endowed wing. Petra feels the pattern closing around his own life. Emotional beat: fear becoming personal.

chapters.title: Detention Economics
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Inside Theo's world: his grandfather Richard's expectations, the weight of the Marsh name, and his growing unease as Petra's findings make sense of half-remembered dinner-table silences. He tests his grandfather with a question about 1994 and gets a warning look. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking under quiet pressure.

chapters.title: Promises in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Late-night archive session turns into something like friendship—Theo admits he hates who he is at school; Petra admits invisibility is its own cage. They agree: if they find proof, they publish it together, after graduation. First almost-laugh, first shared secret. Emotional beat: belonging, tentative and terrifying.

chapters.title: The Hollis Wing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They break into the sealed Hollis Wing during winter break and find a locked cabinet of 'withdrawal files'—expulsion letters rewritten as voluntary departures, hush agreements signed by scared eighteen-year-olds. Someone photographs them entering. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: What Richard Knew
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Richard confronts Theo with the photograph, offering a deal: Petra takes the fall for trespassing, Theo's future stays intact. Theo, cornered, doesn't say no. Petra learns Theo met with Richard and assumes betrayal. The partnership shatters two weeks before prom. Emotional beat: betrayal, and the question of what Theo really chose.

chapters.title: The Night of Prom
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Alone, Petra scans the withdrawal files and the altered yearbooks, uploading everything to an anonymous site timed to prom night. At the dance, he finds Theo—who hands him the cabinet key and confesses he'd been stalling Richard, buying Petra time. The story breaks mid-waltz. Phones light up across the gymnasium. Emotional beat: courage, sacrifice, truth detonating.

chapters.title: The Unedited Edition
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, weeks later. Richard resigns; the board launches an investigation; the six erased students are restored to the record, their names read aloud at assembly. Theo faces his own reckoning, uncertain if forgiveness is possible. Ms. Okonkwo gives them both an A—and Petra, for the first time, signs his full name on the project cover without flinching. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging, justice outside the law, hope.
